reviewer: independent grading agent, separate from service, adapter and recovery builders

findings.finding: Historical receipt validation accepted a nonempty result vector with a different dimension from its immutable source vectors. The orchestration review identified the hypothesis; the independent grader reproduced a one-dimensional result accepted against unchanged two-dimensional source proof.
findings.resolution: Historical proof vectors must be nonempty and have one uniform dimension; the result vector must have that same dimension. Validation uses immutable receipt evidence and does not consult the current embedding model or contract.

reviewed_properties: Canonical intent freezes sorted distinct source IDs, full-record digest preconditions, exact full scope and caller-supplied text; no mutable input alias survives preparation.
All source scopes are checked before any stale-digest or eligibility result; base-only lineage uses exact integer IDs and rejects indirect, duplicate, boolean or floating-point aliases.
Source authority is explicit and never promoted: both lifecycle aliases, expiry, trust, no_merge and merge_policy restrictions fail closed; unknown and typed metadata distinctions are preserved.
Each successful transaction appends one new ID, preserves all original live and archived records and previous receipts, and records complete source snapshots and hashes in the output proof.
Output creation time, fidelity and salience use source minima; stale source summaries are omitted and caller-confirmed result text reaches normal context.
Embedding runs outside writer ownership; model identity and returned vectors are detached and checked against the persisted space before and after preparation and inside each CAS attempt.
Every source and capacity are rechecked on each bounded CAS attempt; unrelated writes rebase and overlapping independently keyed derivations preserve their distinct intended outcomes.
Historical replay validates complete immutable source proof, exact result semantics and proof-bound vector dimensions before accessing current source state, clocks, capacity or models.
Process-death, serialization, real SQLite quota exhaustion, duplicate writer and post-commit acknowledgement or hydration failures preserve all-or-nothing durable outcomes.
The strict provider endpoint preserves existing authorization and returns fixed sanitized error codes; projections and enabled outbox events carry preserved sources and derived output atomically.

Documentation describes independent snapshot lifecycle, non-cascading source changes and explicit operator truth assertions; the maturity inventory remains candidate with no stable API or global production-readiness claim.

limitations: Caller-supplied derived text and trusted/verified source labels remain operator assertions; this feature does not establish semantic truth or authenticate against an attacker who rewrites authoritative history.
Derived memories are independent snapshots. Later source edits, retirement and supersession do not cascade; operators must retire or supersede derived outputs explicitly.
The gate is limited to first-level base memories. Recursive promotion, merge-policy override, semantic deduplication and automatic summarization remain outside the contract.
Declared embedding identity is not model-weight attestation; backend latency remains a caller/provider deadline responsibility.
Full source proofs, journal snapshots and receipts retain history-growth costs; process death and quota tests do not qualify physical power loss on every device.
The original ten production areas remain incomplete. Full-suite and exact-commit CI acceptance are root release gates and feature-specific acceptance does not change production_ready=false.
